item: A merge of the keyword tail that stops half-way is followed by a full rebuild, not by a second addition of the same tail
refs: R306; follow-on of #1565 (final-comparison void); PR pending
summary: refresh_keyword_daily's incremental merge is an UPDATE, an INSERT, the keyword_meta upsert and, last, the last_mention_id watermark, each autocommitted, so a failure or kill after the UPDATE and before the watermark left the tail's counts added while the watermark still pointed before it, and the next refresh at an equal epoch added the same tail again (measured with the INSERT failing after the UPDATE: the next refresh was incremental and 4 of 24 terms differed from a full rebuild). built_epoch is now voided (columnar.VOIDED_BUILT_EPOCH = -1, no corpus epoch, named once and used by both writers and the reader) right before the first write and put back after the watermark, so whatever stops the merge between leaves it voided and the next refresh is a full rebuild; a kill is covered too, which a failure-path write is not. A stop before the first write (the hooks, the tail aggregate) voids nothing. Tests induce the fault at one statement of the real refresh (a proxy raising on the INSERT as a statement error and as MemoryError, a SQLAlchemy OperationalError in the keyword_meta upsert, KeyboardInterrupt standing in for a kill at the watermark write); the causes in the field are inferred, the property after the stop is asserted. If the voiding write itself fails the merge never reaches its UPDATE (a test pins it, fault induced at that write). Red before: 6 of 8 (the 2 controls pass either way). Cost: after an interrupted merge the next refresh is a full rebuild (the persisted build, not the incremental one). Two extra oo_meta writes per incremental merge.
